The given relations imply that the residues \(r \equiv p \pmod{T}\) and \(s \equiv q \pmod{T}\) satisfy \(s^2 \equiv N k^{-1} \pmod{T}\). Because \(T \equiv 3 \pmod{4}\), the two square roots are obtained by exponentiation to the power \((T+1)/4\). The matching residues are then \(r \equiv k s \pmod{T}\). The two candidate pairs \((r,s)\) and \((T-r,T-s)\) produce two candidate sums \(p+q = C T + r + s\). Exactly one of those sums makes the discriminant \((p+q)^2-4N\) a perfect square; the resulting quadratic yields the two prime factors of \(N\). The smaller factor in each row is therefore
\[
9477019,\qquad 13894511,\qquad 10080649.
\]
